sn44.7:2.1: _Loka_ originally meant “light”, hence the sky bright with gods (stars), from which developed the meanings “heaven”, a “world”, and the “cosmos”. Sometimes Vedists believed that an “eternal world” was won by those worthy ([dn1:1.31.5]()). However, the Suttas often discuss the Upaniṣadic notion that the “self and the cosmos are eternal” ([dn1:1.30.1](), [mn102:14.2]()), which confirms that here _loka_ means the “cosmos” as a whole, not a specific heavenly “world”. See also next note.
sn44.7:2.7: “Those who venerate (water, breath, and moon) as finite win only a limited world, whereas those who venerate them as infinite win a world without limit” (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.5.13, Olivelle translation).
